title.narrative: Mitigating the negative effects of the anticipated La Nina induced drought on pastoral and agropastoral livelihoods in Somali and Oromia Regions of Ethiopia

description.narrative: The overarching objective is to mitigate the impacts of the anticipated drought on lives and livelihoods of the most vulnerable population in drought-prone communities in the Somali, South Ethiopia and Oromia regions of Ethiopia, through the provision of critical drought anticipatory animal health services such as vaccination, treatment and refresher training for Community Animal Health Workers (CAHWs) and field level animal health experts. The project is based on the current weather forecast (ICPAC and EMS), while activities are designed according to the National AA Framework for 2024 and expert analysis.Specific objectives:• 640,000 people (128,000 households) supported with vaccination and treatment services against transboundary diseases (approx. 8.2 million small ruminant and around 1.5 million cattle)• Conduct refresher training for 405 CAHWs and 270 Animal Health ExpertsDescription of activities: Output 1: Livestock assets of vulnerable drought prone households are protectedThe project will support 640,000 people (128,000HHs) in drought prone areas with animal health packages that include vaccination and treatment to increase the probability of livestock survival when the anticipated drought intensifies and contribute towards improved livestock body condition and strengthened adaptive capacity to diseases. This intervention will safeguard livestock assets and increase production and productivity, leading to availability of and accessibility to livestock products, especially milk, which is crucial for the nutrition of the most vulnerable household members such as children, pregnant and lactating women and elderly. Further, the project will conduct refresher training of 405 CAHWs and 270 animal health experts to support the animal health service delivery. The project will also support livestock disease surveillance, which is expected to produce disease risk maps depicting endemic areas and at risk of TADs. The project targets to vaccinate about 8,200,000 small ruminants and 1,496,000 cattle and, treat 273,280 small ruminants and 81,984 cattle against various diseases. The treatment service will be provided for 144,440 people (28,888 HH) through voucher-based approach, a system which avoids random distribution and use of veterinary drugs, reduces the risk of AMR, and encourages the private veterinary drug vendors which are the main veterinary drug sources for CAHWs or private animal health service providers in the target areas.
